name: Reentrancy
description: An external call can let another contract re-enter before the caller has finished updating its state.
root_cause: An invariant is temporarily broken across an external call.
mitigation: Update state before external calls and consider a reentrancy guard; examine cross-function paths too.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: A contract interaction transfers control to the called contract, which may call back.
Reentrancy is not limited to Ether transfers; calls to other contracts can also create re-entry paths.
The checks-effects-interactions pattern performs checks, then state changes, then external interactions.

name: Oracle manipulation
description: A manipulable price input can distort collateral valuation or other price-dependent decisions.
root_cause: Contract logic trusts a price without adequate manipulation resistance.
mitigation: Assess feed design, liquidity assumptions, freshness checks and fallback behavior together.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: A price taken from a low-liquidity pool can be influenced by trades against that pool.
A time-weighted price averages observations over an interval; its manipulation resistance depends on liquidity and the averaging period.
An oracle response can be present but too old for its intended use; consumers should check its timestamp.

name: Missing access control
description: A sensitive function without adequate authorization can be called by an unintended account.
root_cause: Permissions are missing or applied inconsistently across privileged entry points.
mitigation: Define roles explicitly and test unauthorized calls for every privileged operation.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Different privileged operations can require different roles.
Role assignment and removal are themselves permission-sensitive operations.
Access control design includes deciding who may grant and revoke permissions.

name: Unchecked external call result
description: Ignoring a failed low-level call can leave the contract proceeding as if an operation succeeded.
root_cause: The caller does not check the success flag returned by a low-level call.
mitigation: Check call outcomes and define explicit failure handling.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Low-level calls expose a success flag that the caller can inspect.
If failure is ignored, subsequent logic may rely on an operation that did not complete.
The failure path needs explicit handling, not only a check of the successful path.

name: tx.origin authorization
description: Authorization based on tx.origin can be abused through a malicious intermediary contract.
root_cause: Authorization checks the transaction origin instead of the intended caller identity.
mitigation: Use an appropriate caller-based authorization design and test intermediary call paths.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: An intermediary contract can call a target within a transaction initiated by a victim.
The transaction origin and the immediate caller can be different addresses.
Caller-based authorization should be evaluated on intermediary call paths, not only direct calls.

name: Unbounded iteration
description: A loop over growing on-chain data can eventually exceed the transaction gas limit.
root_cause: The required work grows without a practical bound.
mitigation: Bound work per transaction or use a carefully designed batching approach.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: A loop whose work depends on storage growth may become too expensive to execute.
Reaching the gas limit can stall a required contract operation.
A loop is not inherently a vulnerability; the relevant issue is whether required work can grow beyond feasible gas.

name: Unchecked arithmetic
description: Arithmetic in unchecked blocks can wrap when a value exceeds its integer range.
root_cause: A calculation assumes bounds that are not enforced.
mitigation: Keep checked arithmetic where possible and test numeric boundary conditions.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Solidity 0.8 and later check arithmetic overflow and underflow by default.
An unchecked block disables these arithmetic checks within its scope.

name: Rounding loss
description: Integer division truncates fractional results and can bias accounting.
root_cause: The design ignores how repeated rounding affects balances or shares.
mitigation: Specify rounding direction and test small values and repeated operations.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Integer division in Solidity rounds toward zero.
An integer result does not retain a fractional remainder.

name: Transaction ordering dependence
description: A pending transaction may be observed and preceded by another transaction that changes its outcome.
root_cause: The design assumes a favorable transaction order.
mitigation: Assess ordering assumptions and use application-appropriate limits or commit-reveal designs.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Visible pending transaction data can influence transactions submitted by other participants.
A transaction-dependent outcome should be assessed under an unfavorable ordering.

name: Predictable randomness
description: Public or influenceable chain values can make an application outcome predictable or biased.
root_cause: The design treats an observable or influenceable input as secure randomness.
mitigation: Use a randomness design appropriate to the threat model and test timing assumptions.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: On-chain state is publicly visible, including state variables declared private.
Block data can be subject to block-builder influence, which matters when it determines an outcome.

name: Signature replay
description: A valid signature may be reused if the verification scheme does not bind and consume its intended context.
root_cause: The scheme omits nonce tracking or adequate domain separation.
mitigation: Bind signatures to the intended domain and action, and consume nonces safely.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Typed-data domain separation can bind signatures to a chain and verifying contract.
Signature recovery identifies a signer; applications still need replay-protection logic.

name: Untrusted delegatecall target
description: Delegatecall executes target code in the calling contract storage context.
root_cause: An untrusted party can influence the target code or its selection.
mitigation: Restrict target selection and review both authorization and storage assumptions.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Delegatecall uses code at another address with the calling contract storage and balance.
Within a delegatecall, the original message sender and value are preserved.

name: Upgrade storage collision
description: An incompatible implementation layout can interpret existing proxy storage incorrectly.
root_cause: An upgrade changes the meaning or ordering of stored fields without preserving compatibility.
mitigation: Validate storage compatibility before approving an implementation upgrade.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Changing the order or types of stored variables can break compatibility during an upgrade.
Storage-layout compatibility must be considered when adding a new implementation.

name: Unprotected initialization
description: An exposed initializer can let an unintended account set privileged state.
root_cause: Initialization is not properly restricted or protected against repeated use.
mitigation: Protect initialization and verify deployment and upgrade initialization paths.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Upgradeable contracts use initializer functions for setup that a constructor would otherwise perform.
Initializer protection prevents the setup function from being executed again.

name: Stale oracle data
description: An old oracle observation can cause a contract to use an outdated price.
root_cause: Consumers omit a freshness policy or fail to enforce it.
mitigation: Validate observation age and define safe behavior when data becomes stale.
severity_note: Illustrative test-data rating; actual severity depends on impact and context.

facts.text: Oracle consumers should validate the timestamp of an observation against a freshness policy.
A price response can be present but too old for its intended use.
